s.t: Dr. Dog released it on their 2010 album Shame, Shame; years later it exploded on TikTok and gave the band their first Platinum record.
s.src: Paste: Dr. Dog Embrace the Present Moment (Kevin Kearney, 16 July 2024)
s.q: a song from 2010's Shame, Shame that exploded on TikTok and led to the band's first Platinum record

s.t: Dr. Dog's Scott McMicken told ACRN.com the song was already eight years old when it came out on Shame, Shame in 2010.
s.q: In an interview with ACRN.com, McMicken said that "Station" and "Unbearable Why" had been originally recorded for other albums, and "Where'd All the Time Go?" was actually eight years old at the time.

s.t: Dr. Dog's song was featured in the second season of the television series Outer Banks.
s.q: Their song "Where'd All the Time Go" was featured in the second season of Outer Banks.

s.t: Dr. Dog played it in a Daytrotter session published on 19 April 2010, alongside ‘I Only Wear Blue’, ‘Station’ and ‘Army of Ancients’.
s.q: I Only Wear Blue / Station / Where'd All The Time Go? / Army Of Ancients

f.t: Their break came when Scott McMicken gave My Morning Jacket's Jim James a CD of their recording Toothbrush, decorated with rainbow sprinkles that caught his eye.
f.src: JamBase: The Year of the Dog (7 March 2007)
f.q: After a MMJ show in Philadelphia, McMicken gave James a CD of Dr. Dog's tape-recorder experiment Toothbrush. The CD was decorated with rainbow sprinkles that caught James's eye so he gave it a shot and loved it.

f.t: Every member has a nickname beginning with T, drawn from their life or personality: former member Andrew ‘Trial’ Jones, for instance, is a licensed attorney.
f.q: each band member has a nickname beginning with the letter T and they have explained that friends of the band also receive nicknames, which are drawn from aspects of their lives and personalities. (Former member Andrew "Trial" Jones, for example, is a licensed attorney.)

f.t: Toby Leaman and Scott McMicken started playing together in eighth grade and never played covers, writing all their own music from the start.
f.q: The origins of Dr. Dog trace back to Toby Mark Leaman and Scott Anthony McMicken first playing music together in eighth grade. The two never played covers, instead opting to write all of their own music.

f.t: The band’s Scott McMicken recorded Big Thief with eight microphones at his Tucson home for Dragon New Warm Mountain I Believe In You, once tracking 13 songs in a day.
f.src: Paste: Dr. Dog Embrace the Present Moment (Kevin Kearney, 16 July 2024)
f.q: McMicken set up eight mics and recorded the band playing live, at one point tracking 13 songs in a single day.

f.t: Toby Leaman has worked as a stone mason, a job he said was ‘really just to stay sane’.
f.q: I actually do have a job — working as a stone mason — but it's really just to stay sane.
